$comment: The fifteen sponsor categories of SPEC §5.3 S10 and PLAN §5.5 S10, keyed by the contracts SponsorCategory enum; a run uses at most six. Names, query strings and public taxonomy URNs only (D29). semantic_query is the /v2/tags semantic search (filter.parents.types=urn:entity:brand, filter.tag.types=urn:tag:genre:brand) that finds a category's tag at runtime; probe names the gate that first ran it (G14 for the original eight, C2 for telecom, fintech and the five Part 8 categories). G14 returned mostly descriptive *:qloo:* tags, which are not taste signals. A verified tag is a brand filter (verified_as brand_filter, never a signal): P5 verified the beer product_category:qloo tag and the energy genre:brand leaf, and the coverage probe (C2) verified one genre:brand leaf per category with a seeded discovery call where every returned brand carried the tag (10/10) and at least 8 in 10 belonged to the category. Carrying a tag is not belonging: a brand whose main line lies in another genre:brand branch (offCategoryBranch in S10, e.g. a fashion house under the beauty tag) is skipped at run time with a notice. Where the runtime lookup's first tag does not fit the category (qsr, fintech, gaming), the verified tag in tags replaces it. A category with no fitting tag keeps tags empty, tag_status unverified and fallback semantic_tag_search: its tag is looked up at run time and labelled as such. Several filter.tags values combine as a union (P5: 20/20 rows carried either energy tag, 9/20 both), so each category lists one tag and S10 sends one category per call. aliases help CLERK and the command grammar map question words to a category.

outdoor_sporting_retail.label: Outdoor and sporting retail
outdoor_sporting_retail.note: C2: no genre:brand tag in the lookup (take 5, then take 20) fits outdoor or sporting retail, and the runtime pick is a home accessories tag. Named fallback: semantic tag search at run time, labelled.

qsr.label: Quick-service restaurants
qsr.note: C2: the taxonomy has no fast-food leaf; the dining leaf (restaurant brands) is the verified filter. The runtime lookup's first tag is a packaged-food tag, so the verified tag replaces it.

fintech.label: Fintech
fintech.note: C2: the runtime lookup's first tag is the whole mobile-app genre; the verified financial-services leaf replaces it.

gaming.label: Gaming
gaming.note: C2: the runtime lookup's first tag is a broader games tag; the verified video game developer leaf replaces it.
